name: thin-main-runnable-core
description: gofib CLI testability: keep main() as a thin flag.Parse + error-exit shim and put all output logic in run(w io.Writer, count int) error, so tests exercise CLI behavior (counts, formats, invalid -n values) via bytes.Buffer instead of os/exec subprocesses. New flags should validate in run and surface errors through main's stderr+exit-1 path.

A previous implementer pass left a compiled 'gofib' binary in the worktree root (gitignored, so the gate stayed green). Hard rule: build smoke checks must not leave binaries behind — use 'go run .' (builds to cache) or build into a temp dir outside the worktree, and remove any stray binary before finishing the pass.
resolution: Binary removed with 'rm -f gofib'; smoke checks now use 'go run .' which builds into the Go cache and never touches the worktree.

name: run-seam-flag-precedence
description: Output-mode precedence in the gofib CLI lives in the run() seam as early-return branches ordered by precedence (version check before the count<1 validation), so every flag combination — including precedence-over-validation cases like -version -n 0 — is unit-testable through run() parameters without process execution. Adding a new output mode means adding one bool parameter, threading 'false' through existing call sites, and putting its branch at its precedence position.
